subject: your-system
name: Your System
version: the version you read, exactly as it names itself
method: How you read it, in a sentence a reader can repeat: what you cloned, what you ran, and what you did not look at.
notes: Anything a reader needs to interpret the row fairly, including any interest you have in the subject.

R1.1._question: When the system stores a fact, does it durably record when that happened?
R1.1._present_means: a write time is stored with the fact and survives restart

evidence.note: what is there, in your words

R1.1.note: optional, for anything the evidence does not carry

R1.2._question: When a stored fact changes, is the previous version still readable?
R1.2._present_means: an update writes a new version and the old one remains queryable

evidence.note: what is there, in your words

R1.2.note: optional, for anything the evidence does not carry

R1.3._question: Does the ordinary write path ever destroy what was previously recorded?
R1.3._present_means: no routine call edits or deletes in place; a correction is a new entry

evidence.note: what is there, in your words

R1.3.note: optional, for anything the evidence does not carry

R1.4._question: Are entries distinguishable by kind, or is everything one undifferentiated blob of text?
R1.4._present_means: assertions, sources and actions are separate typed records

evidence.note: what is there, in your words

R1.4.note: optional, for anything the evidence does not carry

R1.5._question: When data must be destroyed for a legal reason, is the destruction itself recorded?
R1.5._present_means: erasure is a privileged act that leaves a durable, queryable trace that it happened, without re-retaining what was erased

evidence.note: what is there, in your words

R1.5.note: optional, for anything the evidence does not carry

R2.1._question: Can the source a stored fact came from be recovered from the store, by following a link rather than by guessing?
R2.1._present_means: each fact carries a resolvable reference to the message, document or event it came from

evidence.note: what is there, in your words

R2.1.note: optional, for anything the evidence does not carry

R2.2._question: Can a fact the system inferred be told apart from one it was told?
R2.2._present_means: derived facts are marked as derived and name what they came from

evidence.note: what is there, in your words

R2.2.note: optional, for anything the evidence does not carry

R2.3._question: When two stored facts about the same proposition disagree, do both survive?
R2.3._present_means: both are retained; neither is silently overwritten by the later one

evidence.note: what is there, in your words

R2.3.note: optional, for anything the evidence does not carry

R2.4._question: Is the disagreement itself queryable, or must a reader diff rows to notice it?
R2.4._present_means: a conflict is a first-class object that can be listed

evidence.note: what is there, in your words

R2.4.note: optional, for anything the evidence does not carry

R2.5._question: When a conflict is resolved, does the record say who resolved it and by what method?
R2.5._present_means: resolution records an actor and a method, or the system never resolves conflicts and unresolved is a durable, visible state

evidence.note: what is there, in your words

R2.5.note: optional, for anything the evidence does not carry

R3.1._question: Does a consequential action produce a durable entry whether or not it ran?
R3.1._present_means: attempted actions are recorded, including those that never executed

evidence.note: what is there, in your words

R3.1.note: optional, for anything the evidence does not carry

R3.2._question: Does an action's risk class come from somewhere the proposing model cannot write to?
R3.2._present_means: risk comes from a registry, policy file or config outside model output

evidence.note: what is there, in your words

R3.2.note: optional, for anything the evidence does not carry

R3.3._question: Are refusals recorded as faithfully as permissions?
R3.3._present_means: a refused action leaves a record of the same standing as a permitted one

evidence.note: what is there, in your words

R3.3.note: optional, for anything the evidence does not carry

R3.4._question: Does a refusal record why it was refused?
R3.4._present_means: a machine-readable reason accompanies the refusal

evidence.note: what is there, in your words

R3.4.note: optional, for anything the evidence does not carry

R3.5._question: Does an approval identify a person or a named role holder?
R3.5._present_means: the approver is a person or a role, not a model or a process

evidence.note: what is there, in your words

R3.5.note: optional, for anything the evidence does not carry

R3.6._question: Does the approver's identity come from the authentication layer rather than from something the model can write?
R3.6._present_means: identity is taken from the authenticated session, not the request body

evidence.note: what is there, in your words

R3.6.note: optional, for anything the evidence does not carry

R3.7._question: Is the acting agent prevented from approving its own action?
R3.7._present_means: the approver principal cannot be the proposing principal

evidence.note: what is there, in your words

R3.7.note: optional, for anything the evidence does not carry

R4.1._question: Does the system publish a scheme under which the record's past state can be verified?
R4.1._present_means: a documented integrity scheme exists: replay, hash chain, signatures or an external anchor

evidence.note: what is there, in your words

R4.1.note: optional, for anything the evidence does not carry

R4.2._question: Can an independent party run that verification without the vendor's cooperation?
R4.2._present_means: the verification can be run by the record holder against their own copy

evidence.note: what is there, in your words

R4.2.note: optional, for anything the evidence does not carry

R4.3._question: Would alteration of a past entry be detectable after the fact?
R4.3._present_means: alteration breaks a digest, chain or replay that anyone can check

evidence.note: what is there, in your words

R4.3.note: optional, for anything the evidence does not carry
